merge_reason: Kept separate because this is a broad indication-and-drug-class audit of diuretic use in lipedema and comorbid systemic disease.
prompt: Conduct a source-first clinical/pharmacology audit for a Spanish patient-information site about people with lipedema who also have edema or another disease. Determine, by indication and drug class, when diuretics have a legitimate role—heart-failure congestion, nephrotic or other renal edema, cirrhosis/ascites, hypertension, medication-induced edema, and other documented systemic fluid overload—and when they should not be used to treat lipedema adipose tissue or uncomplicated peripheral/lymphatic swelling. Cover loop diuretics, thiazide/thiazide-like agents, mineralocorticoid antagonists and other potassium-sparing agents, acetazolamide, SGLT2 inhibitors as distinct disease-modifying drugs, and over-the-counter or herbal “natural diuretics.” Audit the 2024 German S2k lipedema guideline, the 2021 US Standard of Care, ISL guidance, official Spanish AEMPS/EMA/FDA labels, relevant heart-failure, renal and hepatic guidelines, and the 2024/2025 systematic review of diuretic deprescribing. Separate direct lipedema evidence from adjacent evidence and report study design, population, outcomes, bias and conflicts of interest. Explain why stopping a diuretic can cause transient fluid retention, while distinguishing this from relapse of the underlying indication, worsening blood pressure, renal/hepatic/cardiac decompensation, electrolyte disorders or volume depletion that may be mislabeled as “rebound.” Do not provide patient-specific tapering or dosage advice; give monitoring and red-flag principles only. Identify exact URLs, PMID/DOI and publication dates, open primary sources rather than relying on snippets, and explicitly state whether lipedema-specific trials are absent. Exclude clinics, affiliate pages, supplement marketing and miracle claims. Return an evidence table, contradictions, uncertainties and a concise public-writing recommendation in Spanish. Preserve all research artifacts.
